title: Harness Stall Guard (T2 howto)
desc: How to clear and prevent a stall-guard block: the three resets, how to pick a reset target that actually scores, and why hunting a bypass is the failure the guard exists to catch. Parent: harness-stall-guard. Incidents: harness-stall-guard-ref.
steps: WHAT IT IS: the stall guard fires after roughly 300 seconds of continuous solo tool calls with no user turn. It is not a punishment for working; it is a claim that a session grinding alone that long is almost always thrashing -- a retry loop, speculative file reading, or mechanical work that belongs to a cheap agent. Parent: harness-stall-guard. Dated incidents: harness-stall-guard-ref.

THE THREE RESETS, picked by what the work needs rather than by which is cheapest to type. (1) DELEGATE: any real Agent or Agent.cmd dispatch resets the window, and it is correct whenever the remaining work is mechanical or parallelisable. (2) CONTRIBUTE KNOWLEDGE: a substantive skill edit --add-step scoring 75 or higher resets it immediately, correct when you have just learned something a successor would need. (3) A USER TURN resets it, but waiting is never the plan; it is what happens while you do one of the first two.

PICK THE RESET TARGET BY STEP COUNT, not by topic familiarity. A knowledge-op resets the window only when it scores 75 or above, and an old fat core past roughly 28 steps scores in the low sixties from oversize decay alone no matter how good your new step is, so editing it pays nothing and the block persists. Edit a SMALL, well-tiered, recently-created sibling instead, under about 10 steps, where the score is a flat 100. Measured across four target skills in one session before the pattern was found. Band table: harness-tier-score-guard-howto.

DO NOT HUNT A BYPASS. There is no sanctioned env-var kill switch, and the wk-prefix exemption list is deliberately narrow -- only tools clearly serving knowledge-ification or the public good are exempt, and broadening it is explicitly not sanctioned. A stall block is a signpost to real work: read it once, do exactly what it says, continue. Hunting an escape is the flail pattern the guard exists to interrupt.

THE PREVENTION THAT ACTUALLY WORKS is structural, not reactive: dispatch the mechanical half of the work BEFORE the window closes, then spend the wait knowledge-ifying what you just learned. That habit satisfies the guard as a side effect and never needs a reset at all. Sector-split shape: orchestrate-sectors-parallel-while-knowledgeifying.

NAVIGATION: the guard's own definition and decision rules live in harness-stall-guard; dated incidents and exemption history live in harness-stall-guard-ref; the score band table that decides which reset target actually works lives in harness-tier-score-guard-howto.
2026-09-01: I learned that simply reading a skill does not clear the stall-guard block; I must execute a skill edit with a score of 70 or higher to demonstrate genuine knowledge acquisition.
2026-09-01: To clear the stall guard, always execute a meaningful skill edit. Never use wkappbot exec to wrap a wkappbot skill command.

2026-09-17: appending a new HANDOFF.md letter at the file's bottom does NOT make gates read it -- handoff-manifest-scope.sh treats the FIRST '# HANDOFF --' header in the file as the current letter and stops at the second. An appended letter is structurally invisible to handoff-manifest-gate/handoff-names-gate until the older letter is archived to a dated sidecar and the new letter is moved to the top (same precedent as the existing 16-18/17-18 archives documented at HANDOFF.md's own top).
